## GenBank export

GenBank is the flat file format SnapGene, Benchling, and ApE all read.
Exporting the annotated gene as `.gbk` means you can open it in any of
those tools and see the same exons, guides, primer pairs, and amplicon
that this notebook drew. Each row of the annotation table becomes one
GenBank feature; `build_genbank_features()` maps annotation `feat_type`
values to GenBank's controlled feature vocabulary (for example
`CRISPR_guide` becomes `misc_binding`).

The output file lands in `results/<gene>/`, which is gitignored. The
file contains the full padded genomic sequence in its `ORIGIN` block,
so it must not reach the published `docs/` tree.

```{r genbank-write}
features      <- build_genbank_features(annotation, q, meta)
comment_lines <- build_genbank_comments(meta)

results_dir <- file.path("results", gene_id)
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

safe_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", q$gene_name)
gbk_path  <- file.path(results_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.gbk", q$name, safe_name))
write_genbank(gbk_path, q$gene_name, q$name, q$sequence, features, comment_lines)

cat(sprintf("Wrote %s (%d features)\n", gbk_path, length(features)))
```

Drag the resulting `.gbk` file into SnapGene to see the gene with all
its features annotated, ready for further editing or for designing
follow-up validations.
